title: Specific Technique for Assessing Readiness to Quit Smoking
recommendation_text: Ask patients who smoke these specific questions: 1) 'On a scale of 0-10, how important is it to you to quit smoking?' 2) 'On a scale of 0-10, how confident are you that you could quit if you decided to try?' 3) 'Are you interested in quitting in the next 30 days?' Document responses and tailor intervention based on readiness stage.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine visits for all patients who smoke. Use motivational interviewing techniques based on readiness scores. For those with high importance but low confidence, focus on building self-efficacy. Document stage of change and intervention provided.
expected_outcomes: Improved targeting of cessation interventions, 15-20% increase in quit attempts, and 10-15% improvement in successful cessation rates.
target_population: All patients who use tobacco products
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for reducing tobacco-related healthcare costs.
citation_authors: Fiore MC, Jaén CR, Baker TB, et al.
citation_title: Treating Tobacco Use and Dependence: 2008 Update

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Hypertension
recommendation_text: Use the 'Show-Tell-Show' technique for medication education: 1) Show - demonstrate how to take the medication 2) Tell - explain why it's important and how it works 3) Show - ask the patient to demonstrate back. For patients with adherence issues, implement pill box organization and medication reminder systems tailored to their daily routine.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initiation of therapy and reinforce at follow-up visits. Use actual medication bottles or visual aids. Document specific adherence barriers identified and interventions implemented.
expected_outcomes: 25-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, 10-15 mmHg greater reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to standard education, and reduced hypertension-related complications.
target_population: Patients with hypertension, particularly those with demonstrated non-adherence or complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing hypertension-related hospitalizations and complications.
citation_authors: Conn VS, Ruppar TM, Chase JA, et al.
citation_title: Interventions to Improve Medication Adherence in Hypertensive Patients: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Foot Complications in Diabetes
recommendation_text: Perform the 10-gram monofilament test at 4 specific sites on each foot: 1) Great toe 2) 1st metatarsal head 3) 3rd metatarsal head 4) 5th metatarsal head. Document the number of sites where the patient cannot feel the monofilament. For patients with reduced sensation at any site, implement a comprehensive foot care plan.
implementation_guidance: Perform assessment at least annually for all patients with diabetes. Use a standardized monofilament and replace after 10 patients. Document results in a dedicated foot assessment section of the EHR. Provide immediate education on foot care for abnormal results.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 20-25% more patients at risk for foot complications, 30-40% reduction in foot ulcers with early intervention, and decreased lower extremity amputations.
target_population: All patients with diabetes, particularly those with long-standing disease, poor glycemic control, or previous foot problems
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening (under $5 per patient) with potential for significant cost savings from prevented complications.
citation_authors: Boulton AJ, Armstrong DG, Albert SF, et al.
citation_title: Comprehensive foot examination and risk assessment: a report of the task force of the foot care interest group of the American Diabetes Association

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Understanding in Heart Failure
recommendation_text: Ask patients with heart failure these specific questions about diuretics: 1) 'What time of day do you take your water pill?' 2) 'What do you do if you're going to be away from home when you normally take it?' 3) 'How do you adjust your water pill when you have swelling in your legs or feet?' 4) 'What do you do if you miss a dose?' Document responses and address misconceptions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reconciliation at each visit. Use teach-back method to confirm understanding after education. Document specific misconceptions identified and education provided.
expected_outcomes: Improved self-management of diuretic therapy, 20-25% reduction in heart failure exacerbations, and decreased heart failure-related hospitalizations.
target_population: Patients with heart failure on diuretic therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing costly heart failure hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Riegel B, Moser DK, Anker SD, et al.
citation_title: State of the science: promoting self-care in persons with heart failure: a scientific statement from the American Heart Association

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Asthma
recommendation_text: Implement the 'SIMPLE' approach for inhaler adherence: S (Simplify regimen) - reduce frequency when possible; I (Impart knowledge) - explain how each medication works; M (Modify beliefs) - address concerns about side effects; P (Provide communication) - use clear, non-medical language; L (Leave bias) - avoid blame for non-adherence; E (Evaluate adherence) - ask 'How many doses have you missed in the past week?' Document interventions used.
implementation_guidance: Implement at each visit for patients with asthma. Create a checklist in the EHR to ensure all components are addressed. Schedule more frequent follow-up for patients with identified adherence issues.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% improvement in inhaler adherence rates, 25% reduction in asthma exacerbations, and improved asthma control test scores.
target_population: Patients with asthma, particularly those with poor control or frequent exacerbations
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing emergency department visits and hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Atreja A, Bellam N, Levy SR
citation_title: Strategies to enhance patient adherence: making it simple

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Dehydration in Older Adults
recommendation_text: Assess for dehydration using these specific signs: 1) Tongue dryness - ask patient to stick out tongue and observe for dryness and furrows 2) Axillary dryness - check for moisture in the armpit 3) Sunken eyes - observe for hollowing around the eyes 4) Skin turgor - pinch the skin over the sternum and observe for slow return. Document findings and implement hydration plan for positive signs.
implementation_guidance: Perform assessment during routine visits for older adults, especially during hot weather. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop clear protocols for oral rehydration or IV fluids based on severity.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25-30% more cases of dehydration, earlier intervention to prevent complications, and reduced emergency department visits for dehydration-related issues.
target_population: Older adults, particularly those with cognitive impairment, limited mobility, or taking medications that increase dehydration risk
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant reduction in dehydration-related hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Vivanti A, Harvey K, Ash S
citation_title: Developing a quick and practical screen to improve the identification of poor hydration in geriatric and rehabilitative care

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Schizophrenia
recommendation_text: Ask patients with schizophrenia these specific questions about antipsychotic medications: 1) 'What helps you remember to take your medication?' 2) 'What concerns do you have about your medication?' 3) 'How do you feel your medication is helping you?' 4) 'What side effects bother you the most?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions based on identified barriers.
implementation_guidance: Use a non-judgmental, collaborative approach. Implement during medication management visits. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider long-acting injectable options for patients with significant adherence issues.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of adherence barriers, 20-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, and reduced psychiatric hospitalizations.
target_population: Patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder on antipsychotic medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing costly psychiatric hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Velligan DI, Weiden PJ, Sajatovic M, et al.
citation_title: The expert consensus guideline series: adherence problems in patients with serious and persistent mental illness

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in HIV
recommendation_text: Implement the 'FRAMES' approach for medication counseling: F (Feedback) - provide specific information on adherence importance; R (Responsibility) - emphasize patient's role in success; A (Advice) - give clear recommendations; M (Menu) - offer options for adherence strategies; E (Empathy) - express understanding of challenges; S (Self-efficacy) - build confidence in ability to adhere. Document approach used.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initiation of therapy and reinforce at follow-up visits. Create a checklist to ensure all components are addressed. Schedule more frequent follow-up for patients with adherence concerns.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% improvement in antiretroviral adherence rates, improved viral suppression, and reduced development of drug resistance.
target_population: Patients on antiretroviral therapy for HIV
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for improving treatment outcomes and reducing complications.
citation_authors: Thompson MA, Mugavero MJ, Amico KR, et al.
citation_title: Guidelines for improving entry into and retention in care and antiretroviral adherence for persons with HIV: evidence-based recommendations from an International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care panel

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Orthostatic Hypotension
recommendation_text: Measure blood pressure and heart rate in three positions: 1) After 5 minutes lying supine 2) Immediately upon standing 3) After 3 minutes of standing. Document all readings and calculate the orthostatic change. Implement preventive measures for drops of >20 mmHg systolic or >10 mmHg diastolic upon standing.
implementation_guidance: Perform assessment for patients on antihypertensives, those with fall risk, or those reporting dizziness when standing. Use an automated blood pressure cuff if possible. Document all readings and symptoms experienced during testing.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 15-20% more cases of orthostatic hypotension, appropriate medication adjustments, and reduced fall risk.
target_population: Older adults, patients on multiple antihypertensives, and those with autonomic dysfunction
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant reduction in fall-related injuries and hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Freeman R, Wieling W, Axelrod FB, et al.
citation_title: Consensus statement on the definition of orthostatic hypotension, neurally mediated syncope and the postural tachycardia syndrome

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Epilepsy
recommendation_text: Ask patients with epilepsy these specific questions about antiseizure medications: 1) 'In the past month, how many doses do you think you missed?' 2) 'What time of day is hardest for you to remember your medication?' 3) 'What do you do when you travel or your routine changes?' 4) 'What concerns do you have about your medication?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider electronic reminder systems for patients with memory-related adherence issues.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of adherence barriers, 25-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, and reduced breakthrough seizures.
target_population: Patients with epilepsy on antiseizure medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing emergency department visits and hospitalizations for seizures.
citation_authors: Faught E, Duh MS, Weiner JR, et al.
citation_title: Nonadherence to antiepileptic drugs and increased mortality: findings from the RANSOM Study
